items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: My good friend Eddie Partridge was driving a small bus... I asked him to let me take it home

ctx.x: After a month of practising and seeming to get nowhere, I put the horn under my bed and forgot about it. My good friend Eddie Partridge was driving a small bus at a golf club where he had to go meet different club members that didn't have cars at the street car line and take them back when they had finished playing golf.

Eddie had bought a C melody saxophone quite some time before I bought my cornet-trumpet but I wasn't doing anything with it so I asked him to let me take it home and see if I could do something with it. I tried it a few times but never arrived to the point of playing as much on it as I did on my horn which was not much when I decided to leave it under my bed. The only successful thing I did with the sax was to take all the keys off one day and had a hell of a time getting them back in place again.

I had no idea of being a professional musician when I bought my horn. It was just a desire to play for my own amusement. My father didn't push me to continue trying when I had lost interest in my instrument because I had bought it with money that I had earned and he had not given me one penny to pay for it.
